title: Adaptive micro-shard pacing to align continuous batching with KV-cache defragmentation
creator: Aisha Tan
description:
Problem statement: Continuous batching is increasing GPU memory pressure because small, interleaved requests pin many KV cache entries across micro-regions, producing temporal fragmentation and elevated per-token latency when evictions trigger. This ticket proposes an adaptive micro-shard pacing layer that coordinates request batching windows with opportunistic background defragmentation and GPU-friendly coalescing to reduce fragmentation headroom and OOM risk while preserving end-to-end latency SLOs.

Goals:
- Reduce KV-cache fragmentation-induced extra memory by >=20% on heavy small-request workloads.
- Eliminate transient OOMs during bursty PLG workloads for dedicated pools by increasing effective usable KV utilization.
- Preserve 99th percentile request latency within 10% of baseline for interactive flows.

High-level approach:
1) Micro-shard pacing: group incoming requests into micro-shards (100-500ms soft windows) by token-length and model affinity; emit batching cutpoints that bias kernel dispatches to produce coalesced KV allocations rather than widely scattered inserts. Pacing uses a PID-like controller driven by real-time KV free-runway and observed fragmentation rate.
2) Eviction hysteresis and temporal pinning: introduce an eviction hysteresis tier for recently-accessed KV segments tied to in-flight continuous-batching windows; small batch tails will not immediately evict pinned segments to avoid repeated churn.
3) Opportunistic micro-coalescer: a background, low-priority GPU thread compacts adjacent micro-shards during low-util windows by rewriting contiguous KV entries to a new compact meta-pool with minimal kernel divergence. The compactor prefers slots that would reduce scattered allocations contributing to >80% of fragmentation score.
4) Scheduling alignment: integrate compaction triggers with batching policy so that compaction runs primarily in predicted troughs (derived from recent traffic pattern ACF) or after a canary step when a dedicated pool has safe free margin.
5) Telemetry and safety: add new metrics (fragmentation_score, pinned_fraction, micro_shard_wait_ms, compaction_backpressure) and fail-safes to abort compaction if tail-latency creeps.

Trade-offs considered:
- Increasing batching windows improves coalescing but can add latency for single-request flows; mitigated by soft windows and per-customer latency budget enforcement.
- GPU-side compaction consumes cycles and memory. We run compaction at low priority and only when runway > configured threshold.
- Complexity of coordination across runtime and scheduler; implemented as a thin control plane (pacing controller) that exposes simple signals to the serving runtime rather than rewriting kernel internals.

Implementation plan (phases):
Phase 1 (spike, 1 week): implement a simulation harness that replays production request traces to validate micro-shard windows and compute fragmentation_score delta. Deliverable: spreadsheet + simulation repo.
Phase 2 (prototype, 2 sprints): add pacing controller and micro-shard dispatcher in runtime with no in-GPU compaction (simulate coalescing by reordering allocation patterns). Add telemetry hooks. Deliverable: feature flag gated runtime branch + Grafana dashboard.
Phase 3 (compaction, 2 sprints): implement opportunistic GPU compactor kernel with safety checks and integrate with pacing controller. Run canary in dedicated pool.
Phase 4 (rollout and tuning, 1 sprint): tune PID parameters, eviction hysteresis durations, and thresholds; promote to runtime-1.22 release.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: compaction causes unexpected latency spikes. Mitigation: aggressive backpressure, abort on 95th-tail drift >10%.
- Risk: incorrect coalescing causes read-after-write hazards for KV cache. Mitigation: versioned pointer swap with atomic commit and short grace period.
- Risk: scheduling misprediction leads to wasted compaction cycles. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds and telemetry-driven tuning.

Success metrics:
- Fragmentation score reduced by >=20% on replayed PLG trace.
- Dedicated pool OOM incidents reduced to zero in 30-day canary.
- End-to-end token cost improvement >=5% on affected workloads.

Stakeholders and reviewers: Platform runtime, Scheduler team, Observability (console), and SRE.

Notes: keep all new runtime changes behind feature flags and with explicit opt-in per-dedicated-pool.
